signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry vs Options Downside Skew
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 154.28, holding below its daily SMA20 (157.62), SMA50 (159.69), and SMA200 (158.41) cluster. Overnight indexed swap spreads show a +264bp carry advantage favoring the dollar (SOFR 3.62% vs TONA 0.98%), while the official policy rate gap sits at Fed 3.75% vs BoJ 1.0% (+275bp). Despite this baseline carry support, institutional demand for downside protection remains severe, with 1M 25-delta risk reversals printing at -2.09 put skew alongside an implied volatility of 9.5% against a 30-day realized volatility of 9.3%. Leveraged funds covered +58,042 contracts WoW to reduce their net short to -53,255 (pctl 30, z -0.53) ahead of policy rate decisions, confirming active de-risking rather than carry chasing. The options skew and positioning shift reflect acute repricing as markets price the Bank of Japan raising its policy rate to 1.25% next week. Trade bias: Neutral/bearish USD/JPY; heavy put skew limits carry persistence into the policy meeting. Catalyst: BoJ meeting 18 Sep — policy rate decision. Risk: BoJ leaves the policy rate unchanged at 1.00%, prompting rapid unwinding of options downside hedges.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Crowded Long Positioning Exhaustion
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.7139, testing the immediate support above its rising moving average cluster anchored by the SMA20 at 0.7168 and SMA50 at 0.7069. CFTC data for the week ending 8 Sep shows leveraged funds net long +48,379 contracts, placing positioning at the 93rd percentile of its 52-week historical distribution (z +1.72) with 69.6% gross longs. However, weekly flow stalled with a net reduction of -1,871 contracts WoW even as spot pressed toward cycle highs, signaling late-stage trend exhaustion. Meanwhile, retail sentiment exhibits an opposing 75% short bias, indicating speculative divergence as institutional buyers hesitate. Cash carry offers an RBA-Fed differential of +60bp (RBA 4.35% vs Fed 3.75%), but options markets price a mild put skew of -0.67 in 25d risk reversals. Trade bias: Neutral/defensive AUD/USD; crowded 93rd percentile positioning caps further upside expansion. Catalyst: FOMC rate decision 16 Sep. Risk: Leveraged funds deliver a fresh net expansion above +50k contracts, resuming institutional trend continuation.

signals.title: CHF/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Monetary Divergence
signals.text: The G10 currency strength scorecard registers an active bilateral theme across cross pairs, with JPY leading at an average 1W performance of +0.460% across 7 pairs while CHF lags at -0.506% across 6 pairs, generating a 0.966% spread. Spot CHF/JPY trades at 188.37, well below its BEER fair-value model benchmark of 197.43 (z = -3.36σ). SNB holds at 0.00%. Leveraged funds hold CHF net short positioning at -13,968 contracts in the 12th percentile (z -1.09), confirming persistent spec aversion toward the franc. With retail sentiment holding an extreme 89% long bias on CHF/JPY, positioning remains highly vulnerable to further capitulation. Trade bias: Bearish CHF/JPY; bilateral G10 performance spread and negative policy carry favor JPY dominance. Catalyst: SNB policy meeting 24 Sep. Risk: Spread compresses below 0.80% alongside broad equity market liquidation that restores CHF safe-haven demand.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Bear Flattener Pressure Below Moving Averages
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1554, remaining pinned below its SMA20 (1.1630) and SMA200 (1.1637) while hovering directly over its SMA50 benchmark at 1.1532. The broader macro backdrop is dictated by the US Treasury yield curve operating in a bear-flattener regime, with the 2s10s curve spread at +41.5bp and the US 2Y yield up 1.77% intraday at 4.56%. Benchmark rate differentials firmly benefit the greenback, with Fed 3.75% vs ECB 2.65% maintaining a +110bp nominal advantage (+143bp in SOFR vs €STR OIS carry basis). While European Central Bank communication continues to stress persistent inflation shocks, speculative positioning remains net short EUR at -46,381 contracts (pctl 34, z -0.25). Modest options demand is balanced with 1M implied volatility printing at 5.1% against 4.3% realized vol (+0.8% VRP), keeping directional swings contained within the moving average boundaries. Trade bias: Range/bearish EUR/USD; dollar carry advantage and bear-flattening yields constrain rallies into 1.1630. Catalyst: ECB President Lagarde speech 15:15 UTC. Risk: A daily close above the SMA20/200 cluster at 1.1637 neutralizes downward pressure.
